Artist.value: Rio Blanco Oil Shale Project

ImageDescription.value:
5 volumes : 28 cm
As part of their agreement to lease Colorado Oil Shale Lease Tract C-a, Gulf Oil Corporation and Standard Oil Company (Indiana) were required to design environmental monitoring programs. Programs were implemented in order to determine meteorology and air quality, to describe plant and animal relationships, to characterize soils, and to locate scenic areas and historical artifacts. Revegetation, toxicology, and trace metal studies were added later. Baseline data collected by these programs was utilized to describe the tract's biological and physical aspects, as well as, develop a monitoring program to track changes resulting from oil-shale mining. This report summarizes the progress made by the environmental programs between October 1974 and February 1975
Includes bibliographical references

The San Simon Cienega Wildlife Habitat Area is one of the few remaining areas in the United States that is capable of supporting Mexican duck populations. Continued loss of waterfowl habitat by drainage of marshes, channelization of the Rio Grande and livestock grazing has resulted in a drastic decline of the Mexican duck (Anas diazi) to its present status - an endangered species ... The San Simon Cienega Wildlife Habitat Area lies in both New Mexico and Arizona. The entire area is administered by the Las Cruces District Office ... New Mexico State University was contracted by the Bureau of Land Management to conduct a study on the Mexican duck and its San Simon Cienega habitat in 1966. The final report [was] completed in 1970 ... This research report adequately serves as an inventory of the habitat area
